proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of Email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. The current subject is almost certainly generic enough to pass the Sultanic test badly — something along the lines of "You work hard, so why doesn't it feel like enough?" which a thousand coaches could write. Replace it with a subject grounded in the specific emotional texture of Money Worship: the person who checks their account balance after every purchase not out of prudence but out of reassurance, who ties their self-worth to a number that never quite gets high enough. The new subject should name that specific behaviour, not the category. No question mark (questions underperform in cold-ish automation contexts). No pun. Short enough to read in a notification preview.

proposals.new_text:
---
title: "Why do I promise myself I'll sort my finances on Monday, and then not?"
pubDate: "2026-08-11"
description: "The Monday reset is a ritual, not a plan. Here is what is actually happening when you keep pushing the honest reckoning to next week."
---

Most people who earn well and still feel financially stuck are not short of information. They have read the books. They have opened the spreadsheet at least twice. They know, roughly, what sorting it would involve.

What they are doing on Sunday night — when they tell themselves "I'll look at everything properly on Monday" — is not planning. It is buying quiet. The decision to decide later costs nothing in the moment and restores a few hours of comfort. The problem is that Monday arrives, the day fills up, and the tab stays closed.

Joel sees this in almost every first conversation he has with a client. Not chaos. Not ignorance. A very organised, very capable person who has one specific thing they will not look at directly.

The Monday promise is not a character flaw. It is what happens when the honest reckoning feels more dangerous than the gap itself. The story underneath that delay — what the money actually means, what looking at it might confirm — tends to be the real work.

If you want to find out what pattern is shaping your relationship with money, the quiz takes four minutes and names the thing clearly.

[Take the quiz](https://wayofwealth.co.uk/quiz)

*Joel is an MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner based in the UK.*

proposals.proposal: Rewrite the hero headline and subheadline on the quiz landing page. The current copy is almost certainly a broad value-proposition statement ("Understand your relationship with money") that passes no Sultanic test and names no one specifically. The ICP for this quiz is a person who earns a reasonable salary, checks their bank app more than they would admit, and has a low-grade background awareness that something is off — without being in crisis. The new headline should describe that person's specific interior experience, not the product's benefit. One sentence. No question mark. The subheadline explains the mechanic (four questions, four minutes, named result) so the visitor knows exactly what they are agreeing to.
